title: I Hope This Finds You Well
author: Natalie Sue
blurb:
Really good start but started to drag a bit. Would have been a great short novel. 
Learned I'll never insult people in white text on white background though...

title: What Kind of Paradise
author: Janelle Brown
blurb: I listened to this one and really got into it! Loved the mix of luddite/tech confrontation.

title: Presque Vierge
author: Josée Blanchette
blurb: Les putains d'hommes majeurs qui détruisent les vies de femmes mineures. Frustrant, touchant, mais surtout frustrant

title: Le mensonge du siècle, Anatomie d'une bavure médiatique et judiciaire
author: Daniel Proulx
blurb: Super intéressant d'apprendre sur le context historique et social autour de l'histoire d'Aurore 'l'enfant martyre', de l'évolution des enquêtes criminelles au québec, et des caractérisations imposées aux personnages de son entourage.

title: Meditations for Mortals
author: Oliver Burkeman
blurb: Still wondering if I'll get over it. Seriously would recommend it to anyone that is Type A, overachiever or perfectionist. I will buy the paper version and revisit it!

title: Right Thing, Right Now
author: Ryan Holiday
blurb: As good as other books from Holiday. Encouraging to do the right and virtuous things, even if it isn't easy. About living justly

title: The Woman in Me
author: Britney Spears
blurb: The woman got royally screwed by her entourage but we are all guilty to have followed the trash media laughing at her. Felt like a good dose of humility and was a light reading but informative.

title: Klara and the Sun
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
blurb: Really enjoyed it. Easy read, felt victorian-west andersony (?) in my imagination and I found it rather pleasant!

title: Advice from a Blob:
author: Lennnie
blurb: Very cute and heart-warming cartoon vignettes

title: Subculture Vulture
author: Moshe Kasher
blurb: Fascinating to learn about subcultures I didn't know much about, although I might know more about Burning Man now that I really need... Oh well.

title: Multi
author: Veronique Boisjoly
blurb: Intéressant de lire sur le concept de personne à multi potentiel et multi intérêts, mais j'aurais aimé explorer plus le 'pourquoi' que le 'comment'.

title: Ecrire un roman: Comment devenir écrivain, écrire un livre et le faire publier
author: Marie Vareille
blurb: On sait JAMAIS! haha Super intéressant tout de même!

title: Qimmik
author: Michel Jean
blurb: Bien mais j'ai beaucoup  moins embarqué que Kukum du même auteur.

title: It
author: Alexa Chung
blurb: Meh, felt like a long instagram post by someone cooler than you.

title: How to Dress for Success
author: Edith Head
blurb: Nothing revolutionary but I guess it's the clothing version of fake it till we make it.

title: Manage your day-to-day
author: Jocelyn K. Glei
blurb: Really helped me to understand how to build a routine, especially what to focus on in the morning, and free writing.

title: Design for the Read World
author: Victor J. Papanek
blurb: Read during my Master's studies in design, and definitely a humbling and strong reminder of the importance of the ethical and environmental considerations in the process of design, regardless of the product or services you are defining and putting out in the world.

title: Change by design
author: Brown, Tim
blurb: Interesting approach to innovation through design thinking, written by a pioneer in the domain.

title: This is service design thinking
author: Marc Stickdorn
blurb: A foundational ouvrage for anyone wanting to apply service design methods to their work.

title: Service Design
author: Andy Polaine
blurb: Another crucial read for anyone interested in Service Design, by the founders of Livework, a trailblazing studio in the domain with who I had the pleasure to work with and learn from.

title: Finding Me
author: Viola Davis
blurb:
I listened to Viola via audiobook and I was captivated and moved by her story and storytelling. A tale of resilience, grit, and overcoming adversity. Also a humbling vitrine into divides left by racism and racist policies. 
Definitely recommend!

title: All the Light We Cannot See
author: Anthony Doerr
blurb: Listened to this one and was having a really hard time staying into it. Some chapters where amazing and other passages felt too long. Testing my nonfiction-proned reader's brain a bit.

title: Dear Girls
author: Ali Wong
blurb: Listened to it through night nursing session. Was entertaining to hear it from the author.

title: Killers of the Flower Moon
author: David Grann
blurb:
Is it weird to say this was the soundtrack of my daughter's first month of life? I listened to this bad boy all night long when nursing. 
Loved it, and loved how, compared to the movie, ot provided much more details it provides about the culture and social aspects of the Osage Nation and the role of Mollie politically.

title: Filterworld
author: Kyle Chayka
blurb: Fascinating read about the flattening of culture through social media, the internet and algorithms based interfaces. Loved it.
